correctness.definitions: An overlap is a factor xYxYx with one-letter x and possibly empty Y. Binary k-delicacy means every set of 1 to k position flips creates an overlap; equivalently no other overlap-free same-length word at Hamming distance 1..k. Nonempty finite words n>=1 and exact bit flips used.
correctness.exact_counts: n=13: 60 words; delta histogram {1:44,2:12,3:4}. n=14: 62 words; histogram {1:44,2:14,3:2,4:2}.
correctness.rationale: For each n, exactly enumerating all 2^n binary words and rejecting every factor with period p and length 2p+1 generates O_n. An independent prefix-growth route gives identical sets for n=1..14. The Hamming distance to every distinct O_n word gives maxima <=2 through n=12, 3 at n=13, <=3 through n=13 and 4 at n=14. There are exactly four delta=3 words of length 13 and exactly two delta=4 words of length 14, with the listed reversal/complement orbits; direct flipping of every set of 1..k positions confirms delicacy for extremizers. Thus L_2=13, L_3=14, and complete shortest lists. This exhaustive finite check covers exactly the finite domain required for the two claimed minima, not arbitrary k.
correctness.replay: independent_checks.py and independent_counts.json in the private audit artifact bundle; two independent enumerators and all pairs checked for n=1..14.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general automata/decidability framework can make a finite test possible but does not logically provide the specific exact numerical minima or equality-case lists without an evaluated theorem. The older k=1 classification does not imply k=2 or k=3. No evidenced broader statement actually dominates the result.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new exact first-two generalized-delicacy minima and equality cases. The primary 2021/2022 source names generalized k-delicacy and asks its all-k existence question; it classifies only ordinary k=1. A broader 2022 first-order decidability theorem does not evaluate these minima. OEIS A007777 supplies total overlap-free word counts but not Hamming-isolation distances, while the 2024 isometry paper addresses a different invariant. Targeted exact-string/parameter/alias searches and published mathematical-record searches identified no covering result. Inaccessible plausible 2023 slides are a nontrivial residual priority risk, not a mathematical implication or proof of coverage.
residual_risks: An unindexed computation, unpublished note, or public talk slide could state the same first two finite thresholds and their extremizers.
Plausible 2023 presentation PDF was not retrieved in full, so its potential coverage is undetermined.
The 2024 Hamming-isometric word paper was screened by abstract, not exhaustively read; its stated object is distinct.
Finite certificate does not establish a formula or even existence for all generalized levels k>=4.

value.rationale: These are not arbitrary chosen word lengths: they are the first two natural generalized k-delicacy parameters beyond the explicitly established k=1 theory and are motivated by Przybocki Question 5.1. Exact first-occurrence thresholds with complete minimum witness lists and symmetry classes answer two meaningful initial cases of the established problem. The finite proof is exhaustive (not a sampling extrapolation), though modest in computational scale. A later study of higher k could use the precise initial thresholds and extremizers as base cases; no general all-k theorem is claimed.
